With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
item.description: Scientists have discovered that vitamin C may help prevent potentially cancer-causing chemicals from forming in the stomach after eating foods containing nitrates and nitrites. A new mathematical model suggests that taking vitamin C after meals could reduce these harmful reactions, offering a possible new strategy for lowering cancer risk. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Francophonie summit opens in Cambodia overshadowed by African tensions
item.description: The 20th Francophonie Summit opened on Sunday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, overshadowed by a high-stakes leadership dispute. The International Organisation of the Francophonie is set to elect its next secretary-general on Monday for a four-year term, but escalating friction between Rwanda, which has led the OIF for eight years, and the Democratic Republic of Congo has thrown the summit into crisis. Details by Liza Kaminov. Publicado también por: France 24 - English. Fuente: Africanews.

item.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
item.description: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Kentucky man says agent sold him his own home and pressured him for an extra $85,000
item.description: After hiring estate agent Rick Walters to sell his home, Jason Wagner later bought a property from him. Wagner alleges he was coerced into paying an extra $85,000 above their original agreement. The Kentucky Court of Appeals reinstated many of Wagner's claims against Walters and Lenihan Real Estate, allowing him to proceed in a lower court after previous dismissals. The decision emphasized concerns regarding Walters' financial transactions during the sale. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a surprising genetic connection to spinal degeneration and found that an existing osteoporosis drug can prevent damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines. item.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
item.description: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. item.title: Ethnic minority groups in Wales four times more likely to be target of police facial scans
item.description: Exclusive: South Wales police figures show BAME people accounted for 24% of selected scans in 2025, despite being 7% of population Ethnic minority people are four times more likely than their white counterparts to be chosen for some police facial scans, according to official data, sparking warnings of racial bias. Internal figures released by South Wales police revealed that 24% of people selected by police for facial recognition checks were from ethnic minorities, despite this group making up only 7% of the area’s total population . item.title: New observations challenge evidence for an 'outsize' black hole in the early universe
item.description: A recent reanalysis of the outsize black hole galaxy UHZ1 using existing X-ray data and new infrared observations challenges a previous groundbreaking claim. Three years ago, this galaxy made news for hosting an unusually massive and heavily dust-obscured black hole formed through direct collapse. Led by Fan Zou of the University of Michigan, the new study reports no signs of hidden black hole activity. The paper, published in The Astrophysical Journal on Oct. 14, suggests UHZ1 could be a low-mass, metal-poor, star-forming galaxy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA warns this year's Monster El Niño could be even bigger than legendary 1997 event
item.description: NASA scientists warn that the rapidly intensifying 2026 El Niño could surpass the historic 1997-98 event, which triggered devastating weather extremes around the world. Satellite data reveal striking similarities between the two, raising the possibility of major rainfall and flooding this winter, although the exact impacts remain uncertain. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Uranus and Neptune’s bizarre magnetic fields may finally be explained
item.description: The strange, wildly tilted magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune have puzzled scientists since NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft explored the planets in the 1980s. New simulations suggest that extreme conditions deep inside these icy giants create unusual electrical properties that could explain their magnetic fields. Remarkably, the models indicate that their magnetic poles could shift by tens of degrees within just a few decades, far faster than Earth's. Fuente: ScienceDaily.
